> Sources: `doc/legacy-project-notes.md` and the code. There is no GDD in `doc/` yet, so design
> intent beyond what the code does is `TODO:`.

## What the game is
**The Last Engineer** — a third-person 3D puzzle game (URP, orbital Cinemachine camera). The player
walks modular levels, picks up **nodes** and plugs them into **connections** to open **doors** and
drive **platforms**. A glitch "charge" (0–2) flows between the node in hand and **glitcheable**
objects; the charge decides whether an object is solid, passable or cycling through space.

- **Core loop:** explore a room → read the puzzle → move nodes and glitch charge → satisfy all
  activation sources → door opens → next room / level (via the elevator loading screen).
- **Lose condition:** death by laser or falling into the void → glitch death effect → respawn at the
  last checkpoint. No lives or game over found in code.
- **Win condition:** TODO: no end-of-game condition in `doc/`; the build ends at `4 - NIVEL PLATAFORMAS`.
- **Level flow:** Main menu → Tutorial 1 → Tutorial 2 → HUB → Platforms level. `LVL 1` (1.0–1.3) is a
  new first level in progress, not yet in the build.

## Actors and entities
- **Player** — the engineer; moves, dashes, interacts, carries one node, transfers glitch charge.
- **Node** — pickable object with a glitch level; plugged into connections, carried on the back.
- **Connection** — socket that accepts a node; correct when the node's level matches the required one.
- **Glitcheable** — world object (wall, platform, crystal…) whose glitch level drives a cycle:
  disintegrate → move to next anchor → reintegrate.
- **Door** — opens when all its activation sources (connections, inspectionables) are active.
- **Laser** — beam that powers receptors, can be chained via activators, and kills the player.
- **Moving platform** — follows a route of stations; enabled by a connection.
- **Platform teleport** — teleports the player between platforms; needs a fully glitched node.
- **Inspectionable** — object the player inspects in a separate view to clean corruption from it.
- **Checkpoint capsule** — respawn point.

## Game systems (player-facing)
- **Glitch charge:** Set (left click / □) pushes charge from the node to a glitcheable; Take (right
  click / ○) pulls it back. Tap = 1 charge, hold = the maximum transferable. Charge is conserved.
- **Intangibility:** with level 1, glitcheables become passable for a player holding a level-1 node.
- **Ghost walls:** exist only while the player carries a corrupted node.
- **Inspection minigame:** rotate the object, hold to remove corruption spots with a (gamepad) cursor.
- **Cinematics:** waypoint-driven sequences that take control of the player.
- **Input prompts:** on-screen icons switch between keyboard/mouse and gamepad sprites.

## Glossary (code names)
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `GlitchState` | Charge level: `Clean = 0`, `Intangible = 1`, `Glitched = 2` |
| `GlitchComponent` | Holds an object's charge level; single source of truth for it |
| `GlitchTransferManager` | Static; the only code allowed to move charge (`ExecuteTransfer`, `Preview`) |
| `GlitchPalette` | ScriptableObject with the color per `GlitchState` |
| `Glitcheable` | Object with the glitch cycle FSM (`GlitchIdleState`, `GlitchDisintegratingState`, `GlitchMovingState`, `GlitchReintegratingState`) |
| `TimerController` | Durations of the glitch cycle |
| `NodeController` | A node; `PlayerNodeHandler` is the node in the player's hand |
| `Connection` | Node socket; `_requiredLevel`, `IsCorrectlyConnected`, `OnNodeConnected` |
| `IActivationSource` | Anything a door counts (`Connection`, `Inspectionable`) |
| `DoorController` | Door logic (file `DoorsController.cs`) |
| `IInteractable` / `InteractablePriority` | Something the player can interact with, and who wins when several are in range |
| `PlayerInteractionDetector` | Sole owner of the interactable registry (trigger + line of sight) |
| `IMovablePassenger` | Something a platform carries (the player) |
| `ILaserReceptor` | Something a laser affects (`LaserActivator`, receptors, the player) |
| `CauseOfDeath` | Why the player died: `Teleport`, `Fall`, `Laser` |
| `Inspectionable` / `InspectionType` | Inspectable object; `Panel` or `Battery` |
| `Corruption` / `CorruptionGenerator` / `CorruptionRemover` | Spots to clean in the inspection minigame |
| `LevelLoader` | Scene loading with the elevator screen |
| `ActionMaps` | Input maps: `Player`, `UI`, `PauseUI` |
| HUB | Hub scene connecting the levels |
| Basura | "Trash" — discarded assets folder |

## Key rules and lifecycles
- A glitcheable at level 2 cycles continuously; dropping below 2 interrupts the cycle (except while
  moving — applied on entering reintegration).
- A connection only reports correct when the node's level matches `_requiredLevel` (currently all `Clean`).
- A door opens only when **all** its activation sources are active.
- A platform moves while its connection is correct; disconnecting mid-move decelerates to a stop.
- Death → glitch effect → respawn at `_checkPointPos`.
